findings.description: `local IFS=:` (line 127) is still in effect when `for t in $skipwords` runs, so a multi-word skip list such as "yq jq" is a single token and never equals a basename; only single-tool calls exclude anything. The old `$(IFS=' '; echo "$*")` was split with the same outer IFS, so this is preserved rather than introduced, but the rewrite's comment advertises the line as a working once-built skip list, and the `pw-a-b` directory naming (space to dash on `$*`) shows multi-argument use was intended.
findings.failure_mode: Any test calling `_path_without a b` runs with both tools still on PATH, so a degraded-path assertion passes or fails for the wrong reason and the helper's coverage is vacuous for multi-tool cases.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the list before switching IFS: `local -a skips; IFS=' ' read -r -a skips <<< "$*"`, then `local IFS=:` and test with `for t in "${skips[@]}"` (or `case " $* " in *" $b "*) continue;; esac`). Add one bats case asserting `_path_without yq jq` removes both from the resulting dir.
findings.failure_scenario: Any test calling `_path_without a b` runs with both tools still on PATH, so a degraded-path assertion passes or fails for the wrong reason and the helper's coverage is vacuous for multi-tool cases.

findings.description: The per-file `[ -e ] || [ -L ]` guard now runs before any link from the same PATH directory exists, and the batched `ln` deliberately keeps hard-fail semantics (no `|| true`). Equivalence relies on basenames being unique within a directory as seen by the shim's filesystem. On a host where a PATH dir lives on a case-sensitive volume (Nix store, external case-sensitive APFS) and `$shim` under BATS_TEST_TMPDIR is case-insensitive (macOS default), `Foo` and `foo` both enter the batch; the old loop linked the first and the `-e` test skipped the second, while GNU/BSD `ln` now reports EEXIST for the second and exits 1, which errexit turns into a test failure. GNU, BSD and busybox `ln` all continue past a failed source and accept `--`, so the other batch semantics (first-wins across dirs, dangling-link handling) are unchanged.
findings.failure_mode: Hard test failure on mixed case-sensitivity hosts that passed before the batching change.
findings.suggested_fix: Either tolerate EEXIST only (`ln -s -- "${batch[@]}" "$shim/" 2>"$err" || grep -qv 'File exists' "$err" && exit 1`), or after the batch verify each `b` with the existing `-e || -L` check and let the following `dangling` find() be the single hard assertion.
findings.failure_scenario: Hard test failure on mixed case-sensitivity hosts that passed before the batching change.

findings.description: xtrace is written to the traced shell's stderr. Any construct that redirects the stderr of a function, a `source`, or a subshell sends the trace of everything inside it to /dev/null, and child `bash script` invocations are not traced at all. The hooks under guard use exactly these shapes for their yq/jq calls: `source profile-lib.sh 2>/dev/null && enabled="$(loa_knob … 2>/dev/null || echo false)"` in loa-kf-surface.sh:65-66, `switch="$(loa_knob … 2>/dev/null)"` and `$(bash "$CHECKPOINT" read --json 2>/dev/null | jq …)` in karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh. TOTAL and EXT therefore undercount precisely the spawns the loop optimised, and a regression that adds yq/jq calls inside such a block is invisible to both budgets. The header's claim that the test counts process spawns holds only for top-level, un-redirected commands.
findings.failure_mode: Budgets pass while the real spawn count regresses; the external-tool bound is enforced only on commands whose stderr is not redirected.
findings.suggested_fix: Trace to a dedicated descriptor instead of stderr: `exec {xfd}>"$TRACE_FILE"; env … BASH_XTRACEFD=$xfd bash -x …` (bash honours an inherited BASH_XTRACEFD and the fd survives `2>/dev/null` on functions and sourced files). For nested bash scripts either export `SHELLOPTS=xtrace` or document the gap in the header and in the measured numbers.
findings.failure_scenario: Budgets pass while the real spawn count regresses; the external-tool bound is enforced only on commands whose stderr is not redirected.

findings.anchor: tests/unit/perf-spawn-budget.bats:@test "spawn budget: implement-gate.sh on a Write payload"
findings.description: The header states the live grimoire, .run and config are never read, but the implement-gate, notes-size-guard and run-mode-stop-guard tests pass no config seam. Both hooks supplied in context resolve REPO_ROOT from BASH_SOURCE and read `$REPO_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml` (karpathy honours LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE, kf-surface has LOA_KF_SURFACE_TEST_CONFIG); `PROJECT_ROOT=$proj` in the environment is not a seam either of them consults. If the three traced hooks follow the same pattern, their code path depends on the checked-out repo's knobs: a disabled gate takes an early exit and fails the `canonical_root=` / `notes=` sanity grep, and one extra knob read adds trace lines beyond a +10% headroom that is only +2 lines for notes-size-guard (26→28) and +1 for compat-lib (15→16). Separately, compat-lib's lazy probes make counts toolchain-dependent, and EXT_RE does not match `gawk`, `gsed`, `gdate`, `gstat`, `greadlink`, `grealpath`, `mawk`, `nawk`, so on hosts where compat-lib selects a g-prefixed tool EXT silently drops and the external-tool bound is vacuous.
findings.failure_mode: Red runs on a developer host or after an unrelated config change that are not spawn regressions, or a vacuous EXT bound on Homebrew-coreutils hosts.
findings.suggested_fix: Point each hook at a fixture `.loa.config.yaml` through its own config seam (add LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE-style seams where missing) and assert in the test that the live config path never appears in TRACE_FILE. Extend EXT_RE with the g-prefixed and alternate-awk names. Use `max(mt/10, 3)` as headroom for small budgets and record the measured toolchain (bash, awk, jq, yq versions) in the header so a CI mismatch is diagnosable.
findings.failure_scenario: Red runs on a developer host or after an unrelated config change that are not spawn regressions, or a vacuous EXT bound on Homebrew-coreutils hosts.

findings.description: `_ADAPTER_REGISTRY` is now a derived cache built on first touch, while dispatch (`get_adapter`, `adapter_class_for_type`) reads `_ADAPTER_TYPES` plus `_adapter_class`, which prefers the package global of the class name. Two test seams silently change meaning: `patch.dict('loa_cheval.providers._ADAPTER_REGISTRY', …)` no longer affects dispatch but still affects `cli_adapter_types()`, and `patch('loa_cheval.providers.OpenAIAdapter')` now does affect dispatch (the eager table used to pin the real class). A falsy replacement (`= None`) is also silently discarded by the `or` and the real class is re-imported and re-cached. `cli_adapter_types()` still imports all ten adapter modules on first call, so any cheval dispatch path that consults it for kind:cli admission (its docstring says this is its purpose) re-pays the eager cost and lets a missing optional dependency of an unrelated adapter raise ImportError inside dispatch of a working CLI provider instead of at startup.
findings.failure_mode: Tests that mocked the registry or an adapter attribute keep passing or start passing for the wrong reason; a boto3-less host sees `get_adapter('claude-headless')` fail through `cli_adapter_types()` with an ImportError that no `ConfigError` handler catches.
findings.suggested_fix: Route dispatch through one lazily built mapping (`_registry()` returning the cached dict) so both `adapter_class_for_type` and `cli_adapter_types` read the same object that tests patch; use `name in globals()` rather than truthiness in `_adapter_class`. For `cli_adapter_types()`, derive the headless set from a static `_ADAPTER_AUTH: Dict[str, str]` kept beside `_ADAPTER_TYPES` (asserted equal to the class attribute in a unit test) so admission needs no imports, and wrap the import in `__getattr__` to re-raise as ConfigError with the adapter type and the missing module named.
findings.failure_scenario: Tests that mocked the registry or an adapter attribute keep passing or start passing for the wrong reason; a boto3-less host sees `get_adapter('claude-headless')` fail through `cli_adapter_types()` with an ImportError that no `ConfigError` handler catches.

findings.description: Two places where the byte-for-byte twin claim is host-dependent. (1) `gsub(/\000/, …)` and the octal bracket ranges `[\001-\010…]` are GNU/mawk-1.3.4 behaviour; an awk that rejects a NUL or octal escape in a regex constant exits non-zero and the `2>/dev/null || true` turns a valid known-failures.md into the "parsed ZERO KF entries" WARNING (loud, exit 0, but the surface is lost on that host). The spawn-budget test's fixture is pure ASCII so it would not notice. (2) The comment "GNU cut -c is byte-based in every locale" is true for GNU, but BSD cut (macOS without coreutils) is character-based under UTF-8, so on that host the old cap was 100 characters and the new `substr` cap is 100 bytes and can cut inside a multibyte sequence, emitting an invalid UTF-8 tail into session context.
findings.failure_mode: On an awk without NUL/octal regex support the enabled surface degrades to the warning path for every file; on BSD-cut hosts long non-ASCII symptoms are truncated differently from the reference spec and may end mid-codepoint.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the golden comparison under gawk, mawk and busybox awk in CI (a one-line fixture containing \001, \177 and a 3-byte UTF-8 symptom longer than 100 bytes), replace `/\000/` with a `[^\001-\377]` class or strip NUL via `gsub(/[^\001-\377]/,"")` if any target awk fails, and either state the byte cap as the new contract or trim a trailing partial sequence after `substr`.
findings.failure_scenario: On an awk without NUL/octal regex support the enabled surface degrades to the warning path for every file; on BSD-cut hosts long non-ASCII symptoms are truncated differently from the reference spec and may end mid-codepoint.
